item.title: emberplus_rust
item.description:
Overview

A Rust implementation of the Ember+ protocol, covering both the client (consumer) and server (provider) roles.

Ember+ is a control protocol used in the broadcast and audiovisual industry for communication between equipment (mixers, routers, monitoring systems…).

Features

  • Ember+ client (consumer) implementation
  • Ember+ server (provider) implementation
  • Written in Rust (performance, memory safety)

Why Rust?

Rust provides excellent memory-safety guarantees and performance for a low-level protocol like Ember+, which requires reliable, low-latency communication.

Links

  • GitHub repository
  • Language: Rust

item.title: spacemouse-osc
item.description:
Overview

Bridge between the 3Dconnexion SpaceMouse Compact and the OSC (Open Sound Control) protocol. Lets you use the 6DoF (6 degrees of freedom) controller to drive sound sources in 3D space in real time.

Particularly well suited to controlling spatialisation systems such as Holophonix, Max/MSP or SuperCollider.

Features

  • Read 6DoF data (X/Y/Z translation + rotation) from the SpaceMouse
  • Convert and send data as OSC messages
  • Configurable mappings (axes, OSC addresses, value ranges)
  • Low latency for real-time control

⭐ 14 stars · 1 fork · active

item.title: XCTL_
item.description:
Overview

Reference documentation for the XCTL protocol used by Behringer X-Touch mixing consoles (and compatible surfaces). This MIDI-extended protocol enables bidirectional communication between the control surface and a DAW or custom control system.

This repository collects information gathered through reverse engineering and community documentation — officially undocumented by Behringer.

Contents

  • XCTL message structure
  • Control mapping (faders, encoders, buttons, LEDs, displays)
  • JavaScript implementation examples
  • Comparison with HUI and Mackie Control protocols

Status

⭐ 2 stars · Active · GitHub Pages available

item.title: ALSA-RAVENNA-AES67-Driver
item.description:
Overview

Clone of the ALSA RAVENNA/AES67 driver originally provided by Merging Technologies. This Linux kernel module (LKM) enables the RAVENNA network audio transport protocol (compatible with AES67) within the ALSA subsystem on Linux.

RAVENNA/AES67 is a professional audio-over-IP transport standard used in studios, concert halls and broadcast installations.

Features

  • Linux kernel module (Loadable Kernel Module)
  • RAVENNA/AES67 audio transport over IP
  • Native ALSA integration
  • Compatible with Merging Technologies equipment and other AES67 devices

Status

⭐ 53 stars · 10 forks

item.title: MCxOSCnext
item.description:
Overview

MCxOSCnext is a full rewrite of MCxOSC — evolved from a desktop Electron app into a web microservice deployable via Docker. It bridges Ember+ devices (LAWO MC² consoles, Riedel MediorNet matrices…) with OSC control systems (QLab, Chataigne, Max/MSP…).

┌─────────────┐ ┌──────────────────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐
│ Ember+ │◄───►│ MCxOSC Bridge │◄───►│ OSC │
│ (LAWO MC²) │ TCP │ Backend :3000 UI :80 │ UDP │ (QLab...) │
└─────────────┘ └──────────────────────────┘ └─────────────┘

Architecture

Monorepo with two packages:

  • Backend (Node.js / TypeScript) — Ember+ engine, OSC engine, REST API, WebSocket
  • Frontend (React / Vite) — web UI for configuration and monitoring

Features

  • Bidirectional Ember+ ↔ OSC bridge in real time
  • Web UI for device configuration (IP, ports, mappings)
  • Built-in Ember+ tree explorer
  • Session system — save and reload connection mappings
  • Full REST API + WebSocket for third-party integrations
  • Matrix view for Ember+ routers
  • Docker deployment (one-liner, Compose, Portainer)
  • Compatible with LAWO MC², Riedel MediorNet, and any Ember+ device

Quick start 

# One-liner deployment — no cloning required
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dewiweb/MCxOSCnext/develop/docker-compose.yml | \
 EMBER_HOST=192.168.1.100 docker compose -f - up -d

Open the UI at http://localhost

Status

⭐ 4 stars · active · v2.2.0-beta

Links

  • GitHub repository
  • MCxOSC (original archived version)

item.title: StageNeth
item.description:
Overview

Router OS designed for live performance environments, based on OpenWrt. StageNeth separates audio/video/lighting (AV) streams from the management network and provides the services stage equipment relies on: DHCP, NTP, mDNS, SNMP and PTP.

Features

  • Vue 3 web UI over HTTPS — simple mode (operator) and expert mode (tech)
  • Secured Go API (HttpOnly sessions, argon2id passwords, operator/tech roles)
  • Go network orchestrator — automatic generation of 802.1q VLANs, bridges, firewall, DHCP, QoS/NIC tuning and PTP
  • Per-service configuration — each protocol (Dante, NDI, AES67/RAVENNA, ST 2110, Art-Net, sACN, PTP, AVB, NMOS, MA-Net…) gets its own VLAN, DSCP, priority and MTU
  • Configurable AV trunk and dedicated ST 2110 interface with jumbo frames (MTU 9000)
  • NTP server with DHCP option 42 per VLAN, mDNS reflector across AV VLANs
  • Monitoring: CPU/memory/services, alerts, filterable logs, SNMP v2c/v3 agent, Prometheus metrics

Status

🚧 Active development (v0.2.0-beta) — validate on the bench before any production use.

Links

  • GitHub repository
  • Languages: Go, Vue 3, OpenWrt

item.title: audio-accessibility-system
item.description:
Overview

DIY multichannel audio distribution system for theatres, conference halls and cinemas (~450 seats), designed for audio description, hearing assistance (hard-of-hearing audiences) and multilingual simultaneous interpretation.

Audio is received via AES67/RTP from the mixing console, encoded to HLS by FFmpeg and served to audience smartphones through a PWA — no app to install.

Features

  • Node.js backend + HLS streaming (HTTPS/TLS)
  • AES67/RTP multicast input (L24/48 kHz) from QSYS/Dante consoles
  • Listener PWA + control-room admin UI
  • Security (JWT, CSP, bcrypt), Docker/Portainer deployment
  • CI/CD GitHub Actions → GHCR (amd64 + arm64)

Status

✅ Operational — real-world testing (450 clients) in progress; WebRTC (< 200 ms) planned to reduce latency.

item.title: nextevents
item.description:
Overview

A suite of tools generating slideshows of Les Champs Libres events (Rennes, France) from OpenAgenda data — UHD slides ready for OBS, digital signage and kiosks.

Three variants depending on the infrastructure:

  • nextevents — Debian/Docker server: scrapes leschampslibres.fr + OpenAgenda, renders UHD 3840×2160 PNGs matching the venue’s visual identity (Oldschool Grotesk typeface, per-event pastel background), web UI with gallery and auto-refresh
  • nextevents-desktop — rewritten as a portable PySide6/Qt app (Windows zip, Linux AppImage): same slide generation plus a native fullscreen player, no Docker or server needed
  • nextevents-php — lightweight PHP port for kiosks: self-contained HTML slides (fonts/images in base64), no PNG generation, no dependencies — the kiosk browser does the rendering

Common features

  • Date, duration, venue, price, audience and accessibility (LSF, audio description, surtitling) extracted from OpenAgenda data
  • Native-resolution images, FTP/SMB/local sync
  • Slide of the day, scheduler, gallery

Links

  • nextevents · nextevents-desktop · nextevents-php
  • See also openagenda-slides — the generalized version for any public OpenAgenda agenda

item.title: ptp-monitor
item.description:
Overview

Desktop tool (Qt / PySide6) for passively listening to PTP clock traffic on a production audio-over-IP network — to detect problems and record evidence for vendor support cases.

100% passive: it joins the standard PTP multicast group 224.0.1.129 (UDP 319/320) and listens. It never sends a single PTP packet and cannot disturb the clock election or timing of the network.

Features

  • Dante leader (PTPv1) — who sends Sync, sync interval, jitter (mean/min/max/σ), leader change history
  • AES67 grandmaster (PTPv2) — clock identity, priorities, clock class, steps removed, announce timing
  • Per-source stats — message types, rates, sequence gaps/dupes, silence detection, non-standard PTP domains
  • Malformed packets — unparsable datagrams logged with source IP and full hexdump
  • Evidence logs — chronological JSONL journal + optional full packet capture
  • Network-agnostic — no hard-coded addresses; friendly device names via devices.json, reverse DNS and the IEEE OUI database

Links

  • GitHub repository
  • Language: Python (Qt / PySide6)

The UI is currently in French — i18n contributions are welcome.

item.title: holophonix-animator-blender

  • OSC output /track/{id}/xyz in real time during playback

Requirements

  • OSC libs bundled — no external install needed
